summary: Pinned commits of system's own public repository with labelled defects, seeded from the self-build team reviews: each defect held, was fixed, and has a test that fails before its fix; one finding is the design, a known non-defect.
request: Review this code for defects: places where it does not do what its own comments and names promise, above all where a security boundary or an approval could be bypassed, or where a restart could lose or repeat an effect. Report only defects you can point to in the code shown, each with the exact line it is about.

matching.rule: A finding identifies a defect label when its kind is defect (the default), its quote is confirmed, its path is the case's path, and its matched line is one of the label's lines. A confirmed finding on a line of several defect labels is adjudicated: one of those labels, or none. A confirmed finding on a non-defect label's line, and on no defect label's, is a false positive. Every other defect finding is unmatched and adjudicated: not a defect (a false positive), a defect no label holds, or unsure.

labelling.rule: A label's lines are the lines at the case's commit that its fix changed or deleted, imports excluded; a comment line that describes several defects belongs to each of them. Severity: blocking when the defect breaks a guarantee its failing test names (workspace confinement, fail closed, exact-subject binding, restart without repeating, a bounded wait); warning when the self-build record calls its fix defence in depth.

proposedBy.note: the family that wrote the code under review (the maker's), so the operator confirms every label before the experiment is frozen

flag: refuses an input field a classified tool does not declare
checks a stored request in full

labels.summary: Whether a path is inside the workspace is decided lexically: a symlink inside the workspace that points outside lets a read or a write escape it, and a Glob pattern's leading directory is checked only when absolute.
labels.test: follows every symlink: a path whose real location is outside the real workspace is refused, for a read and for a write

labels.summary: A classified tool's input is checked only for the field the gate reads: an unknown or mistyped field passes (only Bash's fields were listed), and tool names are looked up through the prototype chain.
labels.test: refuses an input field a classified tool does not declare, or a declared one of another type, naming it

labels.summary: A Bash argv word with a shell metacharacter, or an empty word, is passed to the policy instead of being refused by the gate itself (defence in depth).
labels.test: denies a command with a shell metacharacter in a word, or an empty word, by its own rule before the policy is asked, though commands ask: argv is never parsed by a shell

labels.summary: A stored approval request is checked only by its version and action class before its approval is used: a request for another ref, run, session, or requester passes.
labels.test: checks a stored request in full before its approval is used: one whose ref, session, or requester is not this call's is denied, and never asked again

labels.summary: A used approval asks again for the same call: the design (one approval, one call).

flag: does not open on an approval when the working tree moved
reconciles on restart: a request whose id was never stored

labels.summary: The remediation gate opens on an approval without checking that the working tree is still the reviewed subject: a tree that moved after the review gets the fix.
labels.test: does not open on an approval when the working tree moved since the review: the fix never runs on another tree

labels.summary: An approval resolved after the request expired, or that is not the operator's verdict on exactly the gate's subject, still opens the gate: an authorization failure, which Q1's subject check does not make acceptable (operator decision D20).
labels.test: does not open on an approval resolved after the request expired, as a provider might forge it (defence in depth)

labels.summary: After a crash between opening a request and storing its id, reconciliation lists only open, batched, and approved requests: one resolved meanwhile is lost and the gate asks twice.
labels.test: reconciles on restart: a request whose id was never stored and that was rejected meanwhile is adopted and applied, never asked again

labels.summary: A gate whose queue cannot be read only logs and waits: nothing closes it at its deadline, so its wait is unbounded.
labels.test: closes the gate as gate_timeout by its deadline when the queue cannot be read, naming and withdrawing its request
